statement: A predominantly bio-derived porous composite can be designed to hydrate rapidly, retain useful wet mechanical cohesion for a bounded cleaning interval, and subsequently undergo accelerated loss of cohesion.
success_criteria: A literature-calibrated model contains a robust region of parameter space satisfying the lifecycle targets.
The region persists under plausible uncertainty in transport, crosslink kinetics, temperature, ionic conditions, and mechanical loading.
At least two mechanistically distinct material architectures survive virtual falsification before physical validation.
falsifiers: No physically plausible parameter region separates the useful wet lifetime from subsequent disintegration.
Desired behaviour exists only at brittle, implausibly precise parameter combinations.
The mechanism depends on constituents incompatible with the bio-derived/non-persistent design constraints.
notes: CleanCoin is the motivating application; the hypothesis concerns time-programmed wet mechanical lifetime rather than a specific product geometry.
